drhp.business: The Company is principally engaged in manufacturing and processing reclaimed rubber, produced through the recycling and processing of end-of-life rubber products, particularly waste and used tyres and other rubber-based materials. Reclaimed rubber is used, independently or blended with natural and synthetic rubber, in the manufacture of tyres, tubes, belts, footwear, mats, hoses, automotive components and other industrial rubber products. The Company also had a Wind Mill Energy segment, which it sold in June 2026.

drhp.expansion: The Company installed and commissioned an 800 kW rooftop and ground-mounted solar power plant at its Vadodara factory premises in February 2022 for captive use. It subsequently installed and commissioned a 4 MW ground-mounted solar power plant on 6 March 2026 in Desar District, on 59,000 sq. mtr. of land, for captive use, generating 6-7 lakh units monthly. The Company periodically evaluates capital expenditure requirements to improve production efficiency, product quality, capacity utilisation and operational reliability, with future capex to be undertaken based on business requirements, expected returns, availability of resources and prevailing market conditions.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Growth in vehicle ownership, replacement tyre demand and industrial applications is expected to contribute to increased demand for rubber and rubber-based materials.
- Increasing emphasis on recycling and circular economy practices creates a favourable environment for reclaimed rubber manufacturers.
- Reclaimed rubber allows manufacturers to optimise overall raw material cost while maintaining required performance characteristics, which is a demand driver among customers.
- Sustainability-led demand is seen as a structural opportunity for the reclaimed rubber industry over the medium to long term.
- Profitability is influenced by the relationship between selling price of reclaimed rubber and raw material procurement, energy, employee and other operating costs; management is focused on improving this relationship and maintaining operating discipline.
- Management remains cautiously optimistic about medium- to long-term prospects while remaining mindful of commodity price volatility and competitive pressures.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company installed and commissioned an 800 kW rooftop and ground-mounted solar power plant at its Vadodara factory premises in February 2022 for captive use. It subsequently installed and commissioned a 4 MW ground-mounted solar power plant on 6 March 2026 in Desar District, on 59,000 sq. mtr. of land, for captive use, generating 6-7 lakh units monthly. The Company periodically evaluates capital expenditure requirements to improve production efficiency, product quality, capacity utilisation and operational reliability, with future capex to be undertaken based on business requirements, expected returns, availability of resources and prevailing market conditions.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Availability and price of scrap tyres, waste rubber, natural rubber and other raw materials may fluctuate depending upon market conditions.
- Changes in prices of natural rubber, synthetic rubber, carbon black, oil, fuel and other commodities may affect the Company's cost structure and profitability.
- Demand for reclaimed rubber is influenced by the performance of the tyre, automotive and industrial sectors.
- The Company operates in a competitive market, facing competition from domestic manufacturers, imported products and alternative raw materials.
- Manufacturing operations are dependent on energy and fuel; any significant increase in energy costs may adversely affect operating margins.
- Changes in environmental regulations, waste management requirements, labour regulations, taxation and other applicable laws may increase compliance costs or affect operations.
- Dependence on a limited number of major customers, if any, may expose the Company to customer concentration risk.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen the core Rubber Reclaim business by improving operational efficiency, maintaining consistent product quality, strengthening relationships with existing customers, expanding the customer base, optimising raw material procurement, controlling manufacturing and operating costs, and improving capacity utilisation.
- Explore opportunities for product diversification, quality improvement and development of higher-value reclaimed rubber grades based on market demand.
